Each catchment therefore carries its own observed context when selecting climate inputs and calibration periods. The named powerhouse stations preserve their separate identities and operating context.

Eighteenmile sampling and antecedent flow

Sixteen unique lake-study dates are joined to USGS 02186702. The annual 95th percentile of daily mean flow is 134.8 ft³/s. The 9 high-flow days within the 196-day study window carry 24.06% of that window’s observed water volume. Antecedent averages below use the preceding complete three or seven calendar days and exclude the sample date.

Reported upstream discharge in observed flow context

Three original outfalls upstream of gauge USGS 02186702 report 683.718 million US gallons during 2023, equivalent to 2,588,153 m³. Their reported discharge volume is 4.236% of the gauge’s 61,099,554 m³ observed annual water volume.

The three upstream permits are Milliken Pendleton (SC0000477), Pickens Upper (SC0042994) and Pickens Middle (SC0047856). Pendleton-Clemson (SC0035700) remains in the original facility records with its downstream relationship to this gauge. Network membership and reach measures determine that relationship. The monthly percentages compare reported effluent quantities with observed gauge water volume. The annual percentage divides summed annual volumes. October’s larger percentage occurs despite lower reported effluent volume than January, because the river volume is much lower. Transport, retention, travel time and other sources determine receiving-water behavior.

Reported upstream total phosphorus is 949.316 kg over the complete original cohort. Dividing that reported source mass by annual gauge volume gives a gross source-mass/volume index of 0.015537 mg/L. Reported total P mass peaks in June (140.599 kg); the gross mass/volume index peaks in November (0.049749 mg/L). Keeping source mass and river volume beside the index shows both contributions to its seasonal pattern.

Sources and calculation

This self-contained report retains all 59,701 daily rows as compact original-value records. Its charts use those records directly. Original source tables, agency responses, methods and quality flags remain in the accompanying source edition.

Agency queries and original response hashes · Complete hydrology source edition · Basin matching and native 3.20 calibration · Flow and sampling calculation · Complete 29-gauge coverage and quality calculations · Additional 13-gauge source and reference methods · Lake observation report

High-flow volume shares divide sums of actual daily mean discharge; the common conversion factor cancels. The resulting percentages describe water volume. Daily means convert from ft³/s to m³/s by 0.028316846592. Reported concentration, annual nutrient mass and annual sediment mass keep their corresponding measured units and spatial support.

Rebuild from the installed application: node source_tools/build_observed_flow_report.mjs. Interactive controls work offline; print output retains the currently selected hydrograph and complete comparison tables.
